speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The transport sector plays a vital role in Singapore's survival and prosperity, as it brings Singaporeans together, Singapore to the world, and the world to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: COVID-19 has inflicted severe damage on the transport sector.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The Ministry of Transport (MOT) will work with the industry to tide over the COVID-19 pandemic, revive the Changi air hub, strengthen our status as a global hub port, and deliver sustainable and inclusive land transport for our home of the future.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The Changi air hub anchors Singapore's place in the world, making us an attractive node for international business, trade, investment, and tourism.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is even though, geographically, we are not a natural air hub.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We developed into one through the vision of our founding leaders, and decades of enterprise and hard work of workers in the aviation sector.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: However, COVID-19 has decimated air travel and set us back decades.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We cannot take our hub status for granted and assume that we will remain one when global air travel recovers.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Reviving our air hub in a safe way will be a top and immediate priority for MOT.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We have already resumed some transit and transfer services for passengers in a safe way.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will have to take further steps and implement them carefully and progressively, starting with countries or cities which have kept the virus under control, and taking all precautions.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We are helping aviation companies preserve and enhance their core capabilities, and re-skill workers.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We are actively contributing to the International Civil Aviation Organization's (ICAO) COVID-19 global response and recovery efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will take the opportunity when air traffic volume is down to improve our aviation infrastructure, namely developing a three-runway system.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We are reviewing the layout, design, and timeline of Changi Airport Terminal 5 to build a more competitive and resilient terminal for the future.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: While COVID-19 has slowed world trade and disrupted global supply chains, our maritime sector has stayed relatively resilient, and the Port of Singapore continues to serve the trading needs of world markets.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will build on this to further strengthen Singapore's status as a maritime hub and position our port to seize new opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In the coming years, international division of labour may change, global supply chains may shift, and we need to be nimble to adapt to these trends.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We expect Tuas Port to be completed in the 2040s, as planned.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It will be the world's largest fully automated container terminal, able to serve the world's largest container ships.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will step up digitalisation to streamline port clearances, enable just-in-time vessel operations at our port, and standardise and enhance flows of vessel data across ports globally.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The peoples and economies of Singapore and Malaysia are closely intertwined.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The land crossings between us and our closest neighbour have remained open to essential goods and materials throughout the COVID-19 crisis.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Both Governments are progressively restarting travel through the reciprocal green lane and periodic commuting arrangement.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Singapore continues to believe that the HSR is a mutually beneficial project for both countries.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Public transport is key to a greener, fairer, and better Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It emits less carbon dioxide than private transport; it is quieter, safer, and uses less land.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Millions of Singaporeans from all walks of life take public transport every day.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will strive to ensure that public transport stays reliable and affordable for all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will therefore work towards a sustainable and inclusive land transport system for all Singaporeans, in line with our vision of a 45-Minute City with 20-Minute Towns through walk-cycle-ride journeys by 2040.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will continue to build engineering capabilities and invest resources in maintaining the reliability and standard of our public transport system.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In the coming years, we will open new stations and lines almost every year, starting with the remaining stages of Thomson-East Coast Line, to completing Circle Line, and opening Jurong Region Line and Cross-Island Line.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The MRT network will grow from around 230km today to 360km by then.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will continue to improve public transport to better support the less ambulant, and we have begun mobile application trials to help the visually-impaired.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will work with the Public Transport Council and fellow Singaporeans to build a culture of care, where commuters show concern for, and help, fellow commuters with mobility challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Expanding the public transport system to better serve Singaporeans requires major infrastructure and recurrent expenditure.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But this is essential public spending, which has to be carried out with financial prudence.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As transport is part of the sustainable development of Singapore, MOT will work closely with other infrastructure agencies to develop a comprehensive sustainable development plan for Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Improvements to public transport will move us towards a car-lite nation.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will also continue to work on initiatives to promote the adoption of electric vehicles, including efforts to deploy charging infrastructure nationwide.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The lower traffic and new travel patterns brought about by COVID-19 have opened a window of opportunity to re-imagine our road infrastructure.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For example, certain under-used road lanes can be converted to cycling and bus lanes.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: COVID-19 has brought about changes in habits, such as more telecommuting, meaningfully staggered working hours, and greater use of e-commerce.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This has led to more sustainable travel patterns.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will explore ways to make some of these changes permanent.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will support the International Maritime Organization's Strategy on Reduction of Greenhouse Emissions from Ships, and ICAO measures including the Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation.
